## Overview On ROCm with AITER, a plain decode step of a GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layer runs the conv update, the recurrence and the gated RMSNorm as separate launches. This PR runs them as one launch of AITER's Gluon decode kernel through the existing `rocm_aiter_ops.kda_fused_recurrent_packed_decode` wrapper, which the Kimi-K3 layer has used since #57392. Companion prefill change for the same layer: #63568. ## Claims - ROCm, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, CDNA4 or newer (gfx950 is the only architecture run): a plain decode step of a GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layer takes one AITER launch in place of three. No new flag or environment variable; any explicit `--kda-decode-backend` keeps the stock chain. - GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4, MI355X, TP2, one image plus text per request: - `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs: output throughput +5.63 % over concurrency 16–64 (SE 0.80 pp), +13.70 % at concurrency 1, every row positive; - breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs: +3.10 % over concurrency 16–64 (SE 1.13 pp), −1.75 % at concurrency 4 and −2.31 % on the long-prompt row; - GSM8K unchanged within run-to-run variation in both. - Unchanged: CUDA, CPU and gfx942; steps that include a prefill; speculative decoding; non-fp32 recurrent states; other KDA models. ## Validation **Serving.** - Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd` (vLLM `c50aca144`, AITER 0.1.26), whose `kda.py` and `vllm/_aiter_ops.py` equal this PR's base at the time of measurement (`5f63ea461c`). Baseline: that base's `kda.py`; patched: this PR's at the time. Since then the PR's `kda.py` inlines the eligibility check, honours `--kda-decode-backend`, refreshes its decode conv-weight copy after weight writes, rejects an unknown `kda_decode_backend`, and was merged with main's fused q|k|v `conv1d` parameter (#60991); none of these changes what a decode step runs, in the stock chain or the AITER route. - AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), TP2, `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` at revision `b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07`. - Two graph configurations: (i) the flags below; (ii) the same with breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs and the `conv2d` custom op disabled. Without `-conv2d`, MIOpen solver searches for the vision encoder's convolution stalled both arms, so that run's throughput is not reported. - Per configuration, 4 server launches in the order baseline, patched, baseline, patched, each with one discarded warm-up run. 1024 input / 128 output tokens at concurrency 1–64, plus a long-prompt row (5120 / 16, concurrency 16) that weights the steps the kernel does not take. ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 \ --revision b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07 \ --quantization quark --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code # configuration (ii): VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 and # --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE", "custom_ops": ["all", "-conv2d"]}' ``` ```bash # at each concurrency C in 1, 4, 16, 32, 64 with N = 64, 64, 160, 320, 640 prompts vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --model amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 --dataset-name random-mm \ --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \ --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0 \ --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 0}' \ --random-mm-bucket-config '{(512, 512, 1): 1.0}' \ --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $N \ --num-warmups 8 --seed 0 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,99 # long-prompt row: --random-input-len 5120 --random-output-len 16 --max-concurrency 16 --num-prompts 128 ``` | Concurrency | (i) baseline tok/s | (i) patched | (i) change | (ii) baseline tok/s | (ii) patched | (ii) change | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 104.96 | 119.34 | +13.70 % (0.21) | 104.36 | 105.17 | +0.78 % (1.36) | | 4 | 303.60 | 332.39 | +9.48 % (0.39) | 357.45 | 351.19 | −1.75 % (0.27) | | 16 | 777.79 | 828.45 | +6.51 % (0.19) | 769.60 | 799.97 | +3.95 % (4.42) | | 32 | 1020.67 | 1085.43 | +6.34 % (1.58) | 1085.14 | 1113.23 | +2.59 % (0.61) | | 64 | 1298.82 | 1351.09 | +4.02 % (0.72) | 1361.57 | 1399.36 | +2.78 % (0.78) | | 16, long prompt (5120 / 16) | 59.58 | 60.20 | +1.04 % (0.34) | 61.36 | 59.94 | −2.31 % (1.61) | - Output throughput, mean of each arm's two launches; SE of the change in pp in brackets, from the spread between launches (rough with two launches per arm). - TPOT: −2.6 to −13.1 % in (i); −5.0 to −5.7 % at concurrency 16–64 in (ii). - TTFT: no consistent change beyond the launch-to-launch spread, except +5.1 % on the long-prompt row in (ii). - Every patched server log contains `GLM-5.3-Flash KDA decode: AITER single-launch kernel.` once; no baseline log does. KV cache memory is equal across arms (172.7 GiB in (i), 160.54 GiB in (ii)). - `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on the patched breakable-graph server (without `-conv2d`), all rows: no `GPU<->CPU sync detected` line. - GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, strict match, paired McNemar p: - (i): 92.19 → 93.03 % (p 0.315) and 92.80 → 92.04 % (p 0.289); the two baseline launches differ by 0.61 pp (p 0.403); - (ii): 92.04 → 92.57 % (p 0.510) and 92.19 → 92.57 % (p 0.640); baselines differ by 0.15 pp (p 0.910). ```bash lm_eval run --model local-completions \ --model_args "model=amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None" \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 0 --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=512 # lm_eval 0.4.13 ``` **Unit tests.** - `test_aiter_decode_route_follows_replayed_step` (`tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recurrent.py`): - Setup: two real `Glm5NextLinearAttention` layers sharing weights and caches, one with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` and one with `=1`. It calls their `process_weights_after_loading`, as vLLM's loaders do. - It runs in both conv-state layouts: the default and the dim-first one that `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS` selects. The fused kernel receives the conv state with different strides in each. - It captures a breakable PIECEWISE graph of each on an all-decode batch, then replays a mixed step and a decode step. - Mixed step: no fused launch, bit for bit equal to the stock layer. - Decode step: exactly one fused launch of 3 rows; output within 2 bf16 ulp of its largest value; conv state exact; recurrent state within `atol=2e-3, rtol=3e-2`. Kimi-K3's check of this kernel uses `rtol=2e-3` on up to 128 tokens; one of this test's 41.9M state elements reaches 3.8e-3, so `rtol` is that of Kimi-K3's spec-decode check. - Both steps: the fused layer's conv and recurrent state keep their saved values exactly in every slot other than the batch's (1–3). - `test_aiter_decode_reads_refitted_fused_conv` (`tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_conv_weight_refit.py`): - It loads conv weights through the weight loader, refits them through it, and reloads them through the layerwise reload. - After each, the AITER decode must receive `conv1d.weight` in the `[3, width, dim]` layout, at an unchanged address. - It checks that the layer is a deferred attention layer, the condition under which vLLM's loaders call its `process_weights_after_loading`. - The kernel call is replaced, so the test does not need AITER. - MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505` (AITER 0.1.26) with this PR's `vllm/` files over the installed package, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`: - `test_kda_conv_weight_refit.py`: 4 passed; - `test_kda_recurrent.py`: 8 passed (the route test once per layout), 14 skipped (12 need FlashKDA, 2 are NVIDIA-only). - Each check fails when what it covers is removed. These are mutations of this PR's `kda.py`, run once each in the same setup: - no refresh after a shard load: the refit test fails on the first load (`test_kda_conv_weight_refit.py:181`); - no refresh in `process_weights_after_loading`: the refit test fails after the layerwise reload (`:191`), and in both layouts the route test's decode output differs from the stock layer's (`test_kda_recurrent.py:480`; 87 % of elements in the default layout, 83 % in the dim-first one); - the fused route also writing conv-state slot 0: the untouched-slot check fails in both layouts (`test_kda_recurrent.py:479`); - the fused route reading the conv state with the default layout's strides in either layout: the dim-first case's decode output differs (`test_kda_recurrent.py:480`, 78 % of elements); the default case passes. - On the serving image (above), before the review changes: - The route test passed. The decode output's max abs error was 1.562e-02 against a bound of 5.03e-02; recurrent state 3.99e-03. - On main's `kda.py` it failed the decode step: `AssertionError: [1, 1, 1]: fused launches (rows each) []`. - MI355X, serving image, config (i) server with `--kda-decode-backend triton`: starts and serves, and logs no `AITER single-launch kernel` line. - CI: the H200 `GLM5Next` step and its MI355 mirror run `pytest -v -s models/glm5next`. The route test needs AITER's Gluon KDA kernel and is skipped without it, as on CPU. - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.14.0), `typos` (1.51.1): clean. `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.11` (mypy 1.20.2): no issues. ## Details - **Scope.** `Glm5NextLinearAttention` (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/kda.py`), the KDA layer of `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`. The MTP layer is MLA and unaffected. On `main` only `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/kda.py` calls this kernel. - **Eligibility**, decided once in `__init__`: fp32 recurrent state, `head_dim` 128, width-4 conv, a lower bound, no speculative decoding, `--kda-decode-backend` at `auto`, and `rocm_aiter_ops.is_kda_gluon_decode_available()`. An unknown `kda_decode_backend` raises `ValueError`, as in Kimi-K3; `additional_config` bypasses the CLI's choices. An eligible layer logs `GLM-5.3-Flash KDA decode: AITER single-launch kernel.` once. - **Route.** `_forward` takes the fused launch when a step has no prefill and at least one decode. The kernel applies the gated RMSNorm, so an eligible layer passes `out_gate` to `_forward` and `forward` skips `o_norm`; other steps, and profile runs without metadata, apply the norm at the end of `_forward`. The route is chosen in `_forward` because a breakable PIECEWISE graph records `forward` once on a decode-only batch and replays only the eager break against each step's metadata, so a route chosen in `forward` would be fixed at capture. FULL graphs capture `_forward` inline, which is safe because GDN FULL graphs replay uniform decode batches only. - **Weights and indices.** - AITER reads the q|k|v conv weight as a contiguous `[3, width, dim]` tensor, while `conv1d.weight` is `[3·dim, 1, width]`. - An eligible layer keeps that layout in a non-persistent buffer, `decode_conv1d_weight`. It is allocated once in `__init__`, so graphs keep its address, as in Kimi-K3's ROCm layer. - The buffer is refreshed from `conv1d.weight` in two places: - the layer's `process_weights_after_loading`, which `BaseModelLoader.load_model` runs after loading and the layerwise reload runs at its end (`reload_weights` and the weight-transfer engines that use it); - the conv weight loader, after every shard load, for refits that call `load_weights` directly. - The IPC weight cache maps the buffer the daemon filled, so the hook skips it there. - State indices go in as an `[N, 1]` view because the block-table column can be strided. - **Numerics.** AITER keeps the conv and attention outputs in fp32 through the norm; the stock chain rounds to bf16 before `o_norm`. Decode outputs therefore agree to 2 bf16 ulp, not bit for bit. - **Trade-offs.** A step that does not take the kernel pays one extra `copy_` of the layer output, and under breakable PIECEWISE graphs runs `o_norm` eagerly, the likely cause of the (ii) long-prompt result. Fusing only the conv update and the recurrence, keeping `o_norm` in `forward`, would avoid it, at the cost of part of the decode gain and a new `_aiter_ops` wrapper. - **Limits.** gfx1250 passes the probe and has not been run. Without a lower bound the stock kernel falls back to −5.0 while AITER's gate would be unbounded, so that configuration keeps the stock chain. AITER asserts a recurrent slot stride of whole 128-float rows. Not measured: TP 1, 4 and 8; inputs over 5120 tokens; concurrency above 64. - **Weight writes the decode copy does not follow** (from reading the code, not run): - `nccl_m2n`'s direct resharding writes parameters without `load_weights` or a reload, so the copy stays stale. - Sharded RDT counts the buffer as part of the layer, cannot bake the layer, and stops while building its plan. - `--kda-decode-backend triton` keeps the stock chain for both. - Not checked: the tensorizer loader, which overrides `load_model`. - An AITER kernel that reads `conv1d.weight` in place would remove the copy. - **Related PRs.** - #63544 (draft): FlashInfer fused KDA decode for this layer on CUDA, same structure; whichever lands second adapts. - #63070 (draft): breakable CUDA graphs as the ROCm default for GLM-5.3-Flash; configuration (ii) then applies. - #56298 (open): targets the separate q/k/v convs, which #60991 merged into one `conv1d` parameter; this PR no longer interacts with it. - #63071, #63073 (drafts): speculative decoding on this layer, which keeps the stock chain here. This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed every line and ran the tests listed. ---

+def _aiter_kda_decode_runnable() -> bool:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return False
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import get_cdna_version
+
+    return get_cdna_version() >= 4 and rocm_aiter_ops._kda_gluon_decode_importable()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not _aiter_kda_decode_runnable(),
+    reason="Needs AITER's Gluon KDA decode kernel (CDNA4+)",
+)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_aiter_decode_route_follows_replayed_step(dist_init, monkeypatch):
+    """AITER's single-launch decode kernel runs on plain decode steps only.
+
+    Breakable PIECEWISE graphs replay ``_forward`` against each step's metadata,
+    so the route is chosen there. Capture on an all-decode batch, then replay a
+    mixed step (stock chain) and a decode step (one fused launch); a route fixed
+    in ``forward`` fails one of the two. The reference is a layer built without
+    AITER, with the same weights and caches.
+    """
+    from transformers import Glm5NextTextConfig
+
+    from tests.v1.attention.utils import create_vllm_config
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+    from vllm.compilation.breakable_cudagraph import BreakableCUDAGraphCapture
+    from vllm.config import CUDAGraphMode, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.forward_context import ForwardContext, override_forward_context
+    from vllm.models.glm5next.common.kda import Glm5NextLinearAttention
+    from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import GDNAttentionMetadata
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import compute_causal_conv1d_metadata
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    # 32 heads: one rank's share of GLM-5.3-Flash's 64 at tensor parallel 2. With
+    # hidden_size = heads * D, o_proj can be the identity, so the layer output is
+    # the normed core output the tolerances below are set for.
+    heads, max_tokens, num_slots = 32, 64, 80
+    hidden_size = heads * D
+    config = Glm5NextTextConfig(
+        hidden_size=hidden_size,
+        linear_num_heads=heads,
+        linear_head_dim=D,
+        linear_lower_bound=LOWER_BOUND,
+    )
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        model_name="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    layers: dict[str, Glm5NextLinearAttention] = {}
+    try:
+        with (
+            set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config),
+            set_default_torch_dtype(torch.bfloat16),
+            torch.device(device),
+        ):
+            for index, (name, use_aiter) in enumerate((("stock", "0"), ("fused", "1"))):
+                with monkeypatch.context() as env:
+                    env.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER", use_aiter)
+                    rocm_aiter_ops.refresh_env_variables()
+                    layers[name] = Glm5NextLinearAttention(
+                        config, vllm_config, prefix=f"model.layers.{index}.linear_attn"
+                    )
+    finally:
+        rocm_aiter_ops.refresh_env_variables()
+
+    stock = layers["stock"]
+    for name, param in stock.named_parameters():
+        if name.endswith("conv1d.weight"):
+            param.normal_(0, 0.5)
+        elif name == "A_log":
+            param.copy_(torch.log(15 * torch.rand_like(param) + 1))
+        elif name == "dt_bias":
+            param.normal_(0, 0.1)
+        elif name == "o_norm.weight":
+            param.normal_(1, 0.1)
+        elif name == "o_proj.weight":
+            param.copy_(torch.eye(hidden_size))
+        else:  # Input projections.
+            param.normal_(0, param.shape[1] ** -0.5)
+    layers["fused"].load_state_dict(stock.state_dict())
+    conv_shape, state_shape = stock.get_state_shape()
+    saved_caches = (
+        (0.5 * torch.randn(num_slots, *conv_shape, device=device)).bfloat16(),
+        0.1 * torch.randn(num_slots, *state_shape, device=device),
+    )
+    for layer in layers.values():
+        layer.kv_cache = tuple(cache.clone() for cache in saved_caches)
+
+    def metadata(query_lens: list[int]) -> GDNAttentionMetadata:
+        """One request per entry on slots 1, 2, ..., one-token requests first
+        (the builder counts them as decodes). The state indices are a strided
+        column of the block table, as outside FULL graphs."""
+        num_requests, num_decodes = len(query_lens), query_lens.count(1)
+        block_table = torch.zeros(num_requests, 8, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        block_table[:, 0] = torch.arange(1, num_requests + 1, device=device)
+        cu_seqlens = torch.tensor([0, *query_lens]).cumsum(0, dtype=torch.int32)
+        nums_dict, batch_ptr, token_chunk_offset_ptr = compute_causal_conv1d_metadata(
+            cu_seqlens, device=device
+        )
+        return GDNAttentionMetadata(
+            num_prefills=num_requests - num_decodes,
+            num_prefill_tokens=sum(query_lens) - num_decodes,
+            num_decodes=num_decodes,
+            num_decode_tokens=num_decodes,
+            num_spec_decodes=0,
+            num_spec_decode_tokens=0,
+            num_actual_tokens=sum(query_lens),
+            has_initial_state=torch.arange(num_requests, device=device) < num_decodes,
+            non_spec_query_start_loc=cu_seqlens.to(device),
+            non_spec_state_indices_tensor=block_table[:, 0],
+            nums_dict=nums_dict,
+            batch_ptr=batch_ptr,
+            token_chunk_offset_ptr=token_chunk_offset_ptr,
+        )
+
+    def forward_context(step_metadata: GDNAttentionMetadata):
+        return override_forward_context(
+            ForwardContext(
+                {},
+                {layer.prefix: step_metadata for layer in layers.values()},
+                {},
+                cudagraph_runtime_mode=CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE,
+            )
+        )
+
+    launches: list[int] = []
+    launch = rocm_aiter_ops.kda_fused_recurrent_packed_decode
+
+    def record_launch(**kwargs):
+        launches.append(kwargs["mixed_qkv"].shape[0])
+        return launch(**kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        rocm_aiter_ops, "kda_fused_recurrent_packed_decode", record_launch
+    )
+
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    positions = torch.zeros(max_tokens, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    graphs = {}
+    for name, layer in layers.items():
+        static_hidden = torch.zeros(
+            max_tokens, hidden_size, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
+        )
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream), forward_context(metadata([1] * max_tokens)):
+            layer(static_hidden, positions)  # Warm-up, as before every capture.
+            with BreakableCUDAGraphCapture() as capture:
+                output = layer(static_hidden, positions)
+        stream.synchronize()
+        assert capture.num_eager_breaks == 1  # ``_forward`` alone.
+        graphs[name] = (capture, static_hidden, output)
+
+    def replay(name: str, step_metadata: GDNAttentionMetadata, hidden: torch.Tensor):

## Overview On ROCm with AITER, a plain decode step of a GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layer runs the conv update, the recurrence and the gated RMSNorm as separate launches. This PR runs them as one launch of AITER's Gluon decode kernel through the existing `rocm_aiter_ops.kda_fused_recurrent_packed_decode` wrapper, which the Kimi-K3 layer has used since #57392. Companion prefill change for the same layer: #63568. ## Claims - ROCm, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, CDNA4 or newer (gfx950 is the only architecture run): a plain decode step of a GLM-5.3-Flash KDA layer takes one AITER launch in place of three. No new flag or environment variable; any explicit `--kda-decode-backend` keeps the stock chain. - GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4, MI355X, TP2, one image plus text per request: - `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs: output throughput +5.63 % over concurrency 16–64 (SE 0.80 pp), +13.70 % at concurrency 1, every row positive; - breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs: +3.10 % over concurrency 16–64 (SE 1.13 pp), −1.75 % at concurrency 4 and −2.31 % on the long-prompt row; - GSM8K unchanged within run-to-run variation in both. - Unchanged: CUDA, CPU and gfx942; steps that include a prefill; speculative decoding; non-fp32 recurrent states; other KDA models. ## Validation **Serving.** - Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-c50aca14416ef29f6ed0ed256302f30646726dcd` (vLLM `c50aca144`, AITER 0.1.26), whose `kda.py` and `vllm/_aiter_ops.py` equal this PR's base at the time of measurement (`5f63ea461c`). Baseline: that base's `kda.py`; patched: this PR's at the time. Since then the PR's `kda.py` inlines the eligibility check, honours `--kda-decode-backend`, refreshes its decode conv-weight copy after weight writes, rejects an unknown `kda_decode_backend`, and was merged with main's fused q|k|v `conv1d` parameter (#60991); none of these changes what a decode step runs, in the stock chain or the AITER route. - AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), TP2, `amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` at revision `b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07`. - Two graph configurations: (i) the flags below; (ii) the same with breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` graphs and the `conv2d` custom op disabled. Without `-conv2d`, MIOpen solver searches for the vision encoder's convolution stalled both arms, so that run's throughput is not reported. - Per configuration, 4 server launches in the order baseline, patched, baseline, patched, each with one discarded warm-up run. 1024 input / 128 output tokens at concurrency 1–64, plus a long-prompt row (5120 / 16, concurrency 16) that weights the steps the kernel does not take. ```bash VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 vllm serve amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 \ --revision b5688f25491202978c19c4d036eef579f61bbe07 \ --quantization quark --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1}' \ --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \ --no-enable-prefix-caching --trust-remote-code # configuration (ii): VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 and # --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_AND_PIECEWISE", "custom_ops": ["all", "-conv2d"]}' ``` ```bash # at each concurrency C in 1, 4, 16, 32, 64 with N = 64, 64, 160, 320, 640 prompts vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions \ --model amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4 --dataset-name random-mm \ --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 128 \ --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0 \ --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 1, "video": 0}' \ --random-mm-bucket-config '{(512, 512, 1): 1.0}' \ --ignore-eos --request-rate inf --max-concurrency $C --num-prompts $N \ --num-warmups 8 --seed 0 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,99 # long-prompt row: --random-input-len 5120 --random-output-len 16 --max-concurrency 16 --num-prompts 128 ``` | Concurrency | (i) baseline tok/s | (i) patched | (i) change | (ii) baseline tok/s | (ii) patched | (ii) change | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 104.96 | 119.34 | +13.70 % (0.21) | 104.36 | 105.17 | +0.78 % (1.36) | | 4 | 303.60 | 332.39 | +9.48 % (0.39) | 357.45 | 351.19 | −1.75 % (0.27) | | 16 | 777.79 | 828.45 | +6.51 % (0.19) | 769.60 | 799.97 | +3.95 % (4.42) | | 32 | 1020.67 | 1085.43 | +6.34 % (1.58) | 1085.14 | 1113.23 | +2.59 % (0.61) | | 64 | 1298.82 | 1351.09 | +4.02 % (0.72) | 1361.57 | 1399.36 | +2.78 % (0.78) | | 16, long prompt (5120 / 16) | 59.58 | 60.20 | +1.04 % (0.34) | 61.36 | 59.94 | −2.31 % (1.61) | - Output throughput, mean of each arm's two launches; SE of the change in pp in brackets, from the spread between launches (rough with two launches per arm). - TPOT: −2.6 to −13.1 % in (i); −5.0 to −5.7 % at concurrency 16–64 in (ii). - TTFT: no consistent change beyond the launch-to-launch spread, except +5.1 % on the long-prompt row in (ii). - Every patched server log contains `GLM-5.3-Flash KDA decode: AITER single-launch kernel.` once; no baseline log does. It calls their `process_weights_after_loading`, as vLLM's loaders do. - It runs in both conv-state layouts: the default and the dim-first one that `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS` selects. The fused kernel receives the conv state with different strides in each. - It captures a breakable PIECEWISE graph of each on an all-decode batch, then replays a mixed step and a decode step. - Mixed step: no fused launch, bit for bit equal to the stock layer. - Decode step: exactly one fused launch of 3 rows; output within 2 bf16 ulp of its largest value; conv state exact; recurrent state within `atol=2e-3, rtol=3e-2`. Kimi-K3's check of this kernel uses `rtol=2e-3` on up to 128 tokens; one of this test's 41.9M state elements reaches 3.8e-3, so `rtol` is that of Kimi-K3's spec-decode check. - Both steps: the fused layer's conv and recurrent state keep their saved values exactly in every slot other than the batch's (1–3). - `test_aiter_decode_reads_refitted_fused_conv` (`tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_conv_weight_refit.py`): - It loads conv weights through the weight loader, refits them through it, and reloads them through the layerwise reload. - After each, the AITER decode must receive `conv1d.weight` in the `[3, width, dim]` layout, at an unchanged address. - It checks that the layer is a deferred attention layer, the condition under which vLLM's loaders call its `process_weights_after_loading`. - The kernel call is replaced, so the test does not need AITER. - MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-3966924d566340e971a6da313e790d05492aa505` (AITER 0.1.26) with this PR's `vllm/` files over the installed package, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`: - `test_kda_conv_weight_refit.py`: 4 passed; - `test_kda_recurrent.py`: 8 passed (the route test once per layout), 14 skipped (12 need FlashKDA, 2 are NVIDIA-only). - Each check fails when what it covers is removed. These are mutations of this PR's `kda.py`, run once each in the same setup: - no refresh after a shard load: the refit test fails on the first load (`test_kda_conv_weight_refit.py:181`); - no refresh in `process_weights_after_loading`: the refit test fails after the layerwise reload (`:191`), and in both layouts the route test's decode output differs from the stock layer's (`test_kda_recurrent.py:480`; 87 % of elements in the default layout, 83 % in the dim-first one); - the fused route also writing conv-state slot 0: the untouched-slot check fails in both layouts (`test_kda_recurrent.py:479`); - the fused route reading the conv state with the default layout's strides in either layout: the dim-first case's decode output differs (`test_kda_recurrent.py:480`, 78 % of elements); the default case passes. - On the serving image (above), before the review changes: - The route test passed. The decode output's max abs error was 1.562e-02 against a bound of 5.03e-02; recurrent state 3.99e-03. - On main's `kda.py` it failed the decode step: `AssertionError: [1, 1, 1]: fused launches (rows each) []`. - MI355X, serving image, config (i) server with `--kda-decode-backend triton`: starts and serves, and logs no `AITER single-launch kernel` line. - CI: the H200 `GLM5Next` step and its MI355 mirror run `pytest -v -s models/glm5next`. The route test needs AITER's Gluon KDA kernel and is skipped without it, as on CPU. - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` (ruff 0.14.0), `typos` (1.51.1): clean. `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.11` (mypy 1.20.2): no issues. ## Details - **Scope.** `Glm5NextLinearAttention` (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/kda.py`), the KDA layer of `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`. The MTP layer is MLA and unaffected. On `main` only `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/kda.py` calls this kernel. - **Eligibility**, decided once in `__init__`: fp32 recurrent state, `head_dim` 128, width-4 conv, a lower bound, no speculative decoding, `--kda-decode-backend` at `auto`, and `rocm_aiter_ops.is_kda_gluon_decode_available()`. An unknown `kda_decode_backend` raises `ValueError`, as in Kimi-K3; `additional_config` bypasses the CLI's choices. An eligible layer logs `GLM-5.3-Flash KDA decode: AITER single-launch kernel.` once. - **Route.** `_forward` takes the fused launch when a step has no prefill and at least one decode. The kernel applies the gated RMSNorm, so an eligible layer passes `out_gate` to `_forward` and `forward` skips `o_norm`; other steps, and profile runs without metadata, apply the norm at the end of `_forward`. The route is chosen in `_forward` because a breakable PIECEWISE graph records `forward` once on a decode-only batch and replays only the eager break against each step's metadata, so a route chosen in `forward` would be fixed at capture. FULL graphs capture `_forward` inline, which is safe because GDN FULL graphs replay uniform decode batches only. - **Weights and indices.** - AITER reads the q|k|v conv weight as a contiguous `[3, width, dim]` tensor, while `conv1d.weight` is `[3·dim, 1, width]`. - An eligible layer keeps that layout in a non-persistent buffer, `decode_conv1d_weight`. It is allocated once in `__init__`, so graphs keep its address, as in Kimi-K3's ROCm layer. - The buffer is refreshed from `conv1d.weight` in two places: - the layer's `process_weights_after_loading`, which `BaseModelLoader.load_model` runs after loading and the layerwise reload runs at its end (`reload_weights` and the weight-transfer engines that use it); - the conv weight loader, after every shard load, for refits that call `load_weights` directly. - The IPC weight cache maps the buffer the daemon filled, so the hook skips it there. - State indices go in as an `[N, 1]` view because the block-table column can be strided. - **Numerics.** AITER keeps the conv and attention outputs in fp32 through the norm; the stock chain rounds to bf16 before `o_norm`. Decode outputs therefore agree to 2 bf16 ulp, not bit for bit. - **Trade-offs.** A step that does not take the kernel pays one extra `copy_` of the layer output, and under breakable PIECEWISE graphs runs `o_norm` eagerly, the likely cause of the (ii) long-prompt result. Fusing only the conv update and the recurrence, keeping `o_norm` in `forward`, would avoid it, at the cost of part of the decode gain and a new `_aiter_ops` wrapper. - **Limits.** gfx1250 passes the probe and has not been run. Without a lower bound the stock kernel falls back to −5.0 while AITER's gate would be unbounded, so that configuration keeps the stock chain. AITER asserts a recurrent slot stride of whole 128-float rows. Not measured: TP 1, 4 and 8; inputs over 5120 tokens; concurrency above 64. - **Weight writes the decode copy does not follow** (from reading the code, not run): - `nccl_m2n`'s direct resharding writes parameters without `load_weights` or a reload, so the copy stays stale. - Sharded RDT counts the buffer as part of the layer, cannot bake the layer, and stops while building its plan. - `--kda-decode-backend triton` keeps the stock chain for both. - Not checked: the tensorizer loader, which overrides `load_model`. - An AITER kernel that reads `conv1d.weight` in place would remove the copy. - **Related PRs.** - #63544 (draft): FlashInfer fused KDA decode for this layer on CUDA, same structure; whichever lands second adapts. - #63070 (draft): breakable CUDA graphs as the ROCm default for GLM-5.3-Flash; configuration (ii) then applies. - #56298 (open): targets the separate q/k/v convs, which #60991 merged into one `conv1d` parameter; this PR no longer interacts with it. - #63071, #63073 (drafts): speculative decoding on this layer, which keeps the stock chain here. +def test_aiter_decode_route_follows_replayed_step(dist_init, monkeypatch, dim_first):
+    """AITER's single-launch decode kernel runs on plain decode steps only.
+
+    Breakable PIECEWISE graphs replay ``_forward`` against each step's metadata,
+    so the route is chosen there. Capture on an all-decode batch, then replay a
+    mixed step (stock chain) and a decode step (one fused launch); a route fixed
+    in ``forward`` fails one of the two. The reference is a layer built without
+    AITER, with the same weights and caches, in the same conv-state layout.
+    """
+    from transformers import Glm5NextTextConfig
+
+    from tests.v1.attention.utils import create_vllm_config
+    from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops
+    from vllm.compilation.breakable_cudagraph import BreakableCUDAGraphCapture
+    from vllm.config import CUDAGraphMode, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.forward_context import ForwardContext, override_forward_context
+    from vllm.models.glm5next.common.kda import Glm5NextLinearAttention
+    from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.gdn_attn import GDNAttentionMetadata
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import compute_causal_conv1d_metadata
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    device = torch.device("cuda")
+    # 32 heads: one rank's share of GLM-5.3-Flash's 64 at tensor parallel 2. With
+    # hidden_size = heads * D, o_proj can be the identity, so the layer output is
+    # the normed core output the tolerances below are set for.
+    heads, max_tokens, num_slots = 32, 64, 80
+    hidden_size = heads * D
+    config = Glm5NextTextConfig(
+        hidden_size=hidden_size,
+        linear_num_heads=heads,
+        linear_head_dim=D,
+        linear_lower_bound=LOWER_BOUND,
+    )
+    vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+        model_name="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+    )
+    layers: dict[str, Glm5NextLinearAttention] = {}
+    try:
+        with (
+            set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config),
+            set_default_torch_dtype(torch.bfloat16),
+            torch.device(device),

+            for index, (name, use_aiter) in enumerate((("stock", "0"), ("fused", "1"))):
+                with monkeypatch.context() as env:
+                    env.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER", use_aiter)

+            param.normal_(0, 0.1)
+        elif name == "o_norm.weight":
+            param.normal_(1, 0.1)
+        elif name == "o_proj.weight":
+            param.copy_(torch.eye(hidden_size))
+        else:  # Input projections.
+            param.normal_(0, param.shape[1] ** -0.5)
+    layers["fused"].load_state_dict(stock.state_dict())
+    # load_state_dict skips the weight loaders and the non-persistent decode
+    # conv weight; vLLM's loaders end with this hook.
+    for layer in layers.values():
+        layer.process_weights_after_loading(vllm_config.model_config.dtype)

+    # state_len) per slot when dim-first (DS), else (state_len, dim) (SD).
+    conv_shape, state_shape = stock.get_state_shape()
+    if stock._conv_state_dim_first != dim_first:
+        conv_shape = conv_shape[::-1]
+    for layer in layers.values():
+        layer._conv_state_dim_first = dim_first

+        (0.5 * torch.randn(num_slots, *conv_shape, device=device)).bfloat16(),
+        0.1 * torch.randn(num_slots, *state_shape, device=device),
+    )
+    for layer in layers.values():
+        layer.kv_cache = tuple(cache.clone() for cache in saved_caches)
+
+    def metadata(query_lens: list[int]) -> GDNAttentionMetadata:
+        """One request per entry on slots 1, 2, ..., one-token requests first
+        (the builder counts them as decodes). The state indices are a strided
+        column of the block table, as outside FULL graphs."""
+        num_requests, num_decodes = len(query_lens), query_lens.count(1)
+        block_table = torch.zeros(num_requests, 8, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        block_table[:, 0] = torch.arange(1, num_requests + 1, device=device)
+        cu_seqlens = torch.tensor([0, *query_lens]).cumsum(0, dtype=torch.int32)
+        nums_dict, batch_ptr, token_chunk_offset_ptr = compute_causal_conv1d_metadata(
+            cu_seqlens, device=device
+        )
+        return GDNAttentionMetadata(
+            num_prefills=num_requests - num_decodes,
+            num_prefill_tokens=sum(query_lens) - num_decodes,
+            num_decodes=num_decodes,
+            num_decode_tokens=num_decodes,
+            num_spec_decodes=0,
+            num_spec_decode_tokens=0,
+            num_actual_tokens=sum(query_lens),
+            has_initial_state=torch.arange(num_requests, device=device) < num_decodes,
+            non_spec_query_start_loc=cu_seqlens.to(device),
+            non_spec_state_indices_tensor=block_table[:, 0],
+            nums_dict=nums_dict,
+            batch_ptr=batch_ptr,
+            token_chunk_offset_ptr=token_chunk_offset_ptr,

+    def forward_context(step_metadata: GDNAttentionMetadata):
+        # GDNAttentionMetadata does not subclass ForwardContext's AttentionMetadata.
+        return override_forward_context(
+            ForwardContext(
+                {},
+                {layer.prefix: step_metadata for layer in layers.values()},  # type: ignore[misc]
+                {},
+                cudagraph_runtime_mode=CUDAGraphMode.PIECEWISE,
+            )
+        )
+
+    launches: list[int] = []
+    launch = rocm_aiter_ops.kda_fused_recurrent_packed_decode
+
+    def record_launch(**kwargs):
+        launches.append(kwargs["mixed_qkv"].shape[0])
+        return launch(**kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        rocm_aiter_ops, "kda_fused_recurrent_packed_decode", record_launch
+    )
+
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    positions = torch.zeros(max_tokens, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    graphs = {}
+    for name, layer in layers.items():
+        static_hidden = torch.zeros(
+            max_tokens, hidden_size, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
+        )
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream), forward_context(metadata([1] * max_tokens)):
+            layer(static_hidden, positions)  # Warm-up, as before every capture.
+            with BreakableCUDAGraphCapture() as capture:
+                output = layer(static_hidden, positions)
+        stream.synchronize()
+        assert capture.num_eager_breaks == 1  # ``_forward`` alone.
+        graphs[name] = (capture, static_hidden, output)
+
+    def replay(name: str, step_metadata: GDNAttentionMetadata, hidden: torch.Tensor):
+        """The outputs, caches and fused launches of one replay of graph ``name``
+        from the saved caches."""
+        capture, static_hidden, output = graphs[name]
+        launches.clear()
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream), forward_context(step_metadata):
+            for cache, saved in zip(layers[name].kv_cache, saved_caches):
+                cache.copy_(saved)
+            static_hidden.copy_(hidden)
+            capture.replay()
+        stream.synchronize()
+        num_tokens = step_metadata.num_actual_tokens
+        conv, recurrent = (cache.clone() for cache in layers[name].kv_cache)
+        return output[:num_tokens].clone(), conv, recurrent, launches[:]
+
+    # The fused kernel keeps outputs in fp32 where the stock chain rounds to bf16:
+    # 2 bf16 ulp of the largest value. State rtol is Kimi-K3's spec-decode one, as
+    # one of these 41.9M elements reaches 3.8e-3, past its packed-decode 2e-3.
+    fused_rtol = 2 * torch.finfo(torch.bfloat16).eps

+        hidden = torch.randn(max_tokens, hidden_size, device=device).bfloat16()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        stock_out, stock_conv, stock_state, stock_launches = replay(
+            "stock", step_metadata, hidden
+        )
+        fused_out, fused_conv, fused_state, fused_launches = replay(
+            "fused", step_metadata, hidden
+        )

+        assert stock_launches == []
+        assert fused_launches == expected_launches, (
+            f"{query_lens}: fused launches (rows each) {fused_launches}"
+        )
